sum: A week in Lower Mustang: fly to Jomsom, walk to Kagbeni and the shrine of Muktinath at 3,760 m, then follow the Kali Gandaki down through Marpha and Kalopani to Tatopani.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. The way is never hard to find here. What a guide adds is knowledge of the footpaths that avoid the road, which change as bridges wash out and new tracks are cut, and an eye on altitude symptoms at Muktinath.

access: Fly from Pokhara to Jomsom in twenty minutes, on early-morning flights that are cancelled when wind or cloud builds, or take a bus or jeep up the Kali Gandaki road in eight to ten hours. The trek ends at Tatopani, five to six hours by bus from Pokhara through Beni.

photo.a: The village of Kagbeni, with its red monastery, sits among bright green and yellow fields beside the wide gravel bed of the Kali Gandaki, between bare brown hills.
photo.c: Kagbeni and the Kali Gandaki valley

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
road transport to and from the trek

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, a flight or jeep seat up to Jomsom, and a bus back to Pokhara at the end
tips: Walk between six and eleven and keep the afternoons for the villages. The wind makes afternoon walking unpleasant.
Kagbeni is as far north as the Annapurna permit takes you. Beyond the checkpoint you need the Upper Mustang restricted-area permit.
Eat the Thakali dal bhat in Marpha and Tukuche, and try the local apple juice, cider and brandy.
At Muktinath take off your shoes at the temple, ask before photographing pilgrims and walk clockwise round the shrines.
Jomsom has cash machines, but they often fail with foreign cards. Carry cash from Pokhara.

days.t: Fly to Jomsom, walk to Kagbeni
days.note: After the short morning flight, register at the checkpoint in Jomsom and set off up the wide gravel bed of the Kali Gandaki before the wind rises. The way is flat, partly on the road and partly on the riverbed, to Eklebhatti and on to Kagbeni. Spend the afternoon in the old village and its monastery.
why: A jump from 822 m to sleep at 2,810 m in a single day.

n: Show Boat Hotel - Ama chorten cafe

days.note: A steady climb of 950 m up a bare hillside, crossing the road several times, to Khinga and the fortified village of Jharkot. Ranipauwa, where the lodges are, is another hour, with the temple twenty minutes above it. This is a big jump in sleeping height after flying in, so go slowly and drink plenty.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 760 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.note: Visit the temple at dawn, then leave the road for the trail over the ridge to the south, with Dhaulagiri ahead. It drops steeply to the Panda Khola and the Bon village of Lubra, a good lunch stop, then follows the gravel riverbed out to the Kali Gandaki and the road into Jomsom. Expect a headwind for the last hour.

days.t: Jomsom to Marpha by Thini and Dhumba Lake
days.note: A short day on the quiet east bank. Cross the river to Thini, walk on to Dhumba Lake and the monastery on the ridge above it, then descend and follow the east-bank trail to the Tibetan settlement at Chhairo, where a bridge crosses to Marpha. Spend the afternoon among its lanes, monastery and orchards.

Start early to beat the wind. Use the east-bank trail where you can and cross back for Tukuche and its old merchant houses. Beyond Larjung the valley floor is a very wide spread of gravel under the east face of Dhaulagiri, and the path then enters pine forest and climbs gently to Kalopani.

A descent of more than 1,300 m as the valley closes into a gorge between Dhaulagiri and the Annapurnas. Below Lete, footpaths on the east bank avoid much of the road to Ghasa, where permits are checked. Then come the Rupse waterfall, the orange trees of Dana and the hot springs. Split the day at Ghasa if it is hot.

Soak once more in the riverside pools, then take a bus or jeep down the Kali Gandaki to Beni and along the highway through Kusma and Nayapul to Pokhara. Buses leave in the morning. In the monsoon the road below Tatopani is prone to landslides.
